requirements.label: Social Science Gateway Course
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. One social science gateway course, minimum 3 credits: RCSTP 101, or a 200-level introductory course in any social science discipline. Common examples include 200-level courses from RCSTP, WGS, PSYCH, AAS, AMCULT, ENVIRON, and SOC, and the options are not exclusive; confirm your selection with the STP advisor. Per the RC's STP Major Checklist and the LSA bulletin STP major page (effective Winter 2026). Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.

requirements.label: RCSTP 260: Theorizing Knowledge in the Social Sciences
requirements.hint: 3 credits

requirements.label: RCSTP 290: Designing Your STP Major Proposal
requirements.hint: 1 credit

requirements.label: RCSTP Theory Course
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: RCSTP 301 or RCSTP 302

requirements.label: Research Methods Course
requirements.hint: Choose 1. Quantitative: STATS 250, SOC 210, or QMSS 201. Mixed methods: SOC 310. Qualitative: ANTHRCUL 359 or AMCULT 300. Per the RC's STP Major Checklist (linked from the RC Social Theory and Practice page). Other courses may count in consultation with an STP advisor.

requirements.label: Thematic: Social Theory Course
requirements.hint: A second theory course beyond RCSTP 301/302, at least 3 credits, one of the 6 thematic courses (18 credits total, 300 or 400 level with limited exceptions). Matched against the RC's published list of theory focused courses STP students commonly select (Common STP Courses doc, linked from the RC STP Major Checklist). That list is not exhaustive; other courses can count with STP advisor approval. RCSTP 350 must be the Gender, Race, and Education in Feminist Thought topic.

requirements.label: Thematic: Community Engaged-Learning or Practicum Course
requirements.hint: At least 3 credits, one of the 6 thematic courses (18 credits total). Matched against the RC's published list of community engaged/practicum courses STP students commonly select: PCAP, Telling It, SLIP, Semester in Detroit, PALMA, Project Community, and Project Outreach classes, among others (Common STP Courses doc, linked from the RC STP Major Checklist). That list is not exhaustive; other courses and student identified community based internships can count with STP advisor approval. RCSTP 101, 300, 350, and 360 count only as their specific community engaged topics sections.

requirements.label: Thematic Electives
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Minimum 4 elective courses within the 18 credit thematic block (6 courses, 18 credits total, 300 or 400 level with limited exceptions); RCSTP 490 cannot be used. Electives are self selected around your social justice focus, from any department, planned in RCSTP 290 and adjustable with the STP advisor. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.

requirements.label: RCSTP 490: STP Capstone, Senior Project Seminar
Major Total Credits
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Minimum 30 credits from all courses used toward the major (gateway, RCSTP 260 and 290, theory, methods, thematic electives, and capstone; prerequisites excluded). The gateway and thematic portions are self designed with no published list, so this total cannot be counted automatically. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.
